definitions.explanation: A short, memorable phrase used to promote an idea, campaign, or organization. Common in safety campaigns, school activities, advertising, and public awareness efforts in Japan.

examples.japanese: {安全|あんぜん}{標語|ひょうご}を{考|かんが}える。
examples.english: To come up with a safety slogan.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}で{交通|こうつう}{安全|あんぜん}の{標語|ひょうご}を{募集|ぼしゅう}している。
examples.english: The school is soliciting traffic safety slogans.

examples.japanese: {職場|しょくば}の{壁|かべ}に{貼|は}られた{標語|ひょうご}には「{安全|あんぜん}{第一|だいいち}」と{書|か}かれていた。
examples.english: The slogan posted on the workplace wall read 'Safety First.'

notes:
USAGE:
{標語|ひょうご} is a very common word in Japanese workplaces, schools, and public spaces. Safety slogans ({安全|あんぜん}{標語|ひょうご}) are particularly ubiquitous in Japanese construction sites and factories.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {安全|あんぜん}{標語|ひょうご} (safety slogan)
- {交通|こうつう}{安全|あんぜん}{標語|ひょうご} (traffic safety slogan)
- {標語|ひょうご}コンクール (slogan contest)
- {標語|ひょうご}を{掲|かか}げる (to put up a slogan)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- スローガン: loanword "slogan" — used more in political and social movement contexts
- モットー: loanword "motto" — a personal or organizational guiding principle
- キャッチフレーズ: catchphrase — used more in advertising
